record: Introduced the bipartisan ATOMIC Act with Rep. Sara Jacobs, directing Department of Energy National Laboratories to evaluate advanced AI systems for nuclear-related risks and develop containment protocols, mitigation strategies and technical standards.
Introduced the Deepfake Liability Act with Rep. Jake Auchincloss, addressing nonconsensual deepfake pornography and the tools that enable it.

Co-leads the forthcoming bipartisan SAFE AI Act; outline released 19 November 2026 (frontier-lab safety frameworks, incident reporting, federal oversight, emergency authority to stop dangerous models). Not yet introduced.
Office of Rep. Beyer press release, 2026-11-19
grade_reason: Her only risk-related statement, from July 2026, acknowledges serious risks from advancing AI in general terms while introducing a bill to test AI systems for deceptive or unpredictable behavior in nuclear settings. It is a borderline C; a reviewer could reasonably call it D under the 'national security in general terms' ruling.
notes: All six required web searches ran, plus one more on the ATOMIC Act (7 in total). The superintelligence, extinction, pause, China and 'AI safety' searches returned nothing mentioning Maloy. No source found showing she sponsored or co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act or signed any House letter about AI risk outside the centrally handled many-signer letters. The ATOMIC Act quote was re-checked through a page-fetching tool that summarizes pages: Rep. Sara Jacobs's joint release (https://sarajacobs.house.gov/news/press-releases/reps-sara-jacobs-celeste-maloy-introduces-the-atomic-act-to-strengthen-ai-nuclear-security) returned it in full with the closing comma, matching the maloy.house.gov release; still worth a glance at the source. Her quote continues: 'The United States already has the world's leading nuclear security experts in our National Laboratories. This bill builds on that expertise to ensure we can identify emerging threats, strengthen safeguards, and have the information we need to make informed decisions about future AI policy.' (not used; no catastrophic risk named). Co-lead Rep. Sara Jacobs, not Maloy, is quoted on 'Three-Mile Island' and nuclear incidents. A Deseret News article (Eva Terry, 2026-08-06, https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/08/06/celeste-maloy-atomic-act-nuclear-ai/) has Maloy interview remarks such as 'What we want to know is what capabilities AI has' and that she wants to 'get AI regulations right' and be 'clear eyed about some of the risks'; the fetch tool returned these only as truncated excerpts, so they are not quoted as statements; they are level D at most. Search coverage also paraphrased her as not wanting to over-regulate AI (no direct quote seen). The bill's listed risks include generating sensitive nuclear information (misuse) and AI deceptive or unpredictable behavior (AI itself); neither is described as catastrophic in her words. I did not open the Deepfake Liability Act release (would be D). Later pages of her press release list and her House videos on AI liability were not checked.
